title: The Shop Window Bride
premise: A display mannequin asks the player to stop a wedding scheduled in 1912.
pressure: A mannequin in a Ferndale shop window begs you to stop a wedding planned for 1912. Behind its veil lies a modern bus ticket.
investigate: Find out which wedding the mannequin remembers
success: The archive reveals the ceremony never happened because both people chose to leave town together.
failure: A clockwork cough closes the window before you learn the names; the bus ticket remains.
help: Ask the shopkeeper before interfering with strangers
helpOutcome: The display is changed respectfully, and an elderly visitor recognizes a family photograph.

title: The Cow Who Owns the Theater
premise: An elegantly dressed cow has inherited a very specific deed.
pressure: A well-dressed cow owns the theater by inheritance and intends to stage a new play, but the board says hooves cannot sign contracts.
investigate: Review the deed and old theater books
success: The deed is valid except for one clause signed fifty years in the future.
failure: Ink smears the last page. You can still prove the theater belonged to the family.
help: Help the company rehearse with its unusual patron
helpOutcome: The cow attends opening night and votes to pay the stage crew a proper wage.

title: Victorian House of Cards
premise: A tourist attraction's floor plan is rearranged by drawing cards.
pressure: Each card drawn from an antique deck rearranges a Victorian house's rooms. The tour guide is trapped between staircases that never meet.
investigate: Map the rooms in the order the cards were drawn
success: The route traces an old shoreline beneath Ferndale's painted storefronts.
failure: The door relocates before you can mark it; the guide leaves a trail of chalk.
help: Get visitors out before the next card turns
helpOutcome: Everyone reaches the garden without sacrificing the guide's dignity for a photo.

title: The Pie Contest with a Second Jury
premise: An unseen panel awards prizes based on regrets, not flavor.
pressure: An unseen jury tastes pies and awards prizes for regrets they claim the baker should confess. The public judges want to disqualify the invisible votes.
investigate: Ask the second jury to explain its scoring
success: The regrets describe a town event that will not occur until next year's fair.
failure: The pie tin rings like a bell and the unseen panel withdraws without a verdict.
help: Let bakers choose what stories they tell
helpOutcome: The town awards the pie for flavor and keeps confessions voluntary.

title: Parade Float of Future Regrets
premise: A float features the player's decisions with embarrassing accuracy.
pressure: The parade float contains a miniature scene from your own weekend, including an embarrassing decision you have not yet made.
investigate: Check who built the miniature future
success: The model's paint includes a county seal that does not exist and a meeting date not yet set.
failure: The float takes a turn and the figures swap places, leaving two competing predictions.
help: Help the children finish the parade safely
helpOutcome: They move the dangerous wheel and the spectators celebrate a float rather than a prophecy.

title: The River Lodge Has No Exit
premise: A conference room exits into every other conference room at once.
pressure: A conference room at a Fortuna lodge opens into another identical room no matter which door you take. A staffer is delivering coffee in a loop.
investigate: Trace the fire-exit plan and the door numbers
success: One door opens onto a meeting held fifteen years from now about restoring the Eel River.
failure: You return to the lobby empty-handed but discover a keycard from a room never built.
help: Help everyone leave together and check the exits
helpOutcome: The staff organize a slow headcount, and the impossible corridor reluctantly releases them.

title: An Extremely Civilized Were-Bear
premise: A genial local asks for help with noise complaints during full moons.
pressure: A courteous were-bear has received a noise citation for roaring on full moons. He brings letters from neighbors who disagree about the sound.
investigate: Check the time and source of the alleged noise
success: The roar precedes its own echo by several seconds and coincides with a distant flood siren.
failure: Your meter records nothing beyond wind, but a neighbor confirms the timing.
help: Mediate a practical quiet-hours agreement
helpOutcome: The bear helps install safer lighting and promises a warning bell before the next transformation.

title: The Hardware Store Crop Circle
premise: A perfect circle appears in the aisle of extension cords.
pressure: A crop circle appears in the hardware aisle among extension cords. The owner blames students; the cords hum with a frequency nobody bought.
investigate: Measure the circle before merchandise is moved
success: Its geometry matches the proposed plan for a new radio relay on the hills.
failure: A mop erases the pattern; the hum remains on the store's emergency battery.
help: Help the owner reopen the aisle without blaming anyone
helpOutcome: Workers reroute the cables and the shoppers finish their errands in peace.

title: The Lost Receipt of Destiny
premise: A cashier recognizes a receipt for an object that has not been invented.
pressure: A cashier produces a receipt for an invention that does not exist. The receipt names a customer who will not be born for years.
investigate: Cross-check the printed part numbers
success: They describe a device for measuring habitat health that could be built from today's components.
failure: The thermal paper fades, but the cashier remembers the strange serial prefix.
help: Make sure the cashier isn't penalized for the glitch
helpOutcome: The manager documents the event and refunds the customer without demanding an impossible explanation.

title: The Eel River Forecast Desk
premise: A volunteer weather station forecasts emotional conditions alongside rainfall.
pressure: The Eel River volunteer forecast station reports both rainfall and the emotional weather of nearby residents. A coming storm is labeled APOLOGY.
investigate: Compare the predictions with actual river measurements
success: The station has forecast a fast rise at a crossing absent from current hazard maps.
failure: The sensors fail during the test, but the volunteer flags a real drainage obstruction.
help: Help the volunteers publish an accessible warning
helpOutcome: Residents receive clear high-water advice with none of the ominous emotional labels.

title: The Tree with a Reception Desk
premise: A hollow redwood hosts a receptionist for the forest's impossible visitors.
pressure: A receptionist sits inside an immense redwood, registering visitors whose species and century are both optional fields.
investigate: Inspect the check-in ledger with consent
success: The next arrival is listed as a future park ranger seeking an unbuilt public path.
failure: The ledger closes when you ask too much; the receptionist still offers a trail map.
help: Support a welcome policy that protects the grove
helpOutcome: The strange visitors keep a quiet route and ordinary hikers get clear signs.

title: The Giant's Smaller Older Brother
premise: An enormous silhouette insists the real giant is just off-trail.
pressure: A vast shadow claims its older brother is smaller and standing behind the next redwood. Every witness sees a different scale.
investigate: Take measurements without leaving the safe trail
success: The shadow's feet match a cliff formation miles away, projected at the wrong time of day.
failure: The silhouette fades and your measuring tape snaps back to ordinary length.
help: Keep the gawkers from damaging the roots
helpOutcome: A ranger persuades the crowd to stay on the boardwalk and let the giant be unphotographed.

title: A Roadside Attraction for Ghost Cars
premise: Invisible tourists keep buying tickets to an abandoned exhibit.
pressure: Invisible tourists queue at an abandoned roadside attraction and pay for tickets with neatly folded blank paper.
investigate: Read the guestbook for evidence of their route
success: Every guest signed the same future date and named a bridge removed years ago.
failure: A gust tears out the page, but the empty ticket machine prints one more stub.
help: Help a neighbor turn the site into a safe rest area
helpOutcome: The old booth becomes a free map-and-water stop for travelers nobody can quite see.

title: The Redwood Rings of Tomorrow
premise: A fallen log records two more summers than have occurred.
pressure: A fallen redwood has two extra growth rings, each showing a summer nobody remembers. A contractor proposes to sell the slice as proof of prophecy.
investigate: Compare the rings with local climate records
success: One extra season contains evidence of drought mitigation that has not yet begun.
failure: The sample splinters before a count is complete; the pattern survives in a careful rubbing.
help: Protect the log until stewards decide its fate
helpOutcome: Volunteers cover the exposed wood and agree the forest should not be auctioned for a miracle.

title: The Family Portrait in the Bark
premise: A tree's scars resemble a family the player has just met.
pressure: A redwood scar resembles a family you met earlier, including a child they have not introduced. The faces change whenever the light changes.
investigate: Sketch the marks from two directions
success: A new figure appears beside the family at a future reunion, carrying an unfamiliar tool.
failure: Your pencil snaps and the light shifts. The family portrait is gone but the scar is still there.
help: Ask before showing the strange likeness
helpOutcome: The family chooses to view the sketch privately and leaves their own memory of the grove.

title: The Backwoods Crop that Talks Back
premise: A remote garden's sentient scarecrow wants employment protections.
pressure: A talking scarecrow is the only worker willing to tend a backwoods garden in the rain. Its owner says a thing made of straw cannot bargain.
investigate: Ask what work the scarecrow actually performs
success: The ledger reveals a hidden irrigation leak the scarecrow has patched for months.
failure: The scarecrow goes silent at the owner's approach but leaves a careful repair list.
help: Negotiate rest and credit for the strange worker
helpOutcome: The gardener posts fair duties and builds a dry shelter the scarecrow can enter.

title: The Moonshine of Mixed Timelines
premise: A homebrewed drink makes two contradictory memories equally convincing.
pressure: Two neighbors share a homebrew recipe and remember contradictory versions of the same harvest. Neither memory is evidence about the other person.
investigate: Compare the stories against signed records
success: A shipping slip belongs to a future cooperative that neither neighbor yet trusts.
failure: The labels peel off the jars and you cannot establish which account is older.
help: Help the neighbors decide what they know together
helpOutcome: They preserve both stories and agree to share a meal without forcing a verdict.

title: The Farmer's Unmarked Helicopter
premise: A low-flying craft is piloted by something that understands zoning rules.
pressure: A helicopter without registration follows the same line over a garden, piloted by someone obsessed with zoning maps.
investigate: Record its path from publicly accessible ground
success: The flight traces the outline of a proposed conservation easement no one has yet drawn.
failure: Cloud cover swallows the vehicle, but the ground crew sees the last waypoint.
help: Help residents ask for transparent flight notices
helpOutcome: The neighbors draft a calm request instead of accusing one another of secret deals.

title: The River Stone Adoption Agency
premise: A family insists their pet rock is the rightful heir to a ranch.
pressure: A family insists a river stone has inherited a ranch. The county clerk has never handled probate for a rock and is trying hard to be polite.
investigate: Inspect the will and the stone's markings
success: The marks are a flood-high-water record predicting the ranch's most vulnerable field.
failure: The ink smudges on the old envelope. The family still explains why the stone mattered.
help: Help the heirs make a fair shared-use plan
helpOutcome: They protect the riverbank and keep the stone on the mantel instead of using it as a weapon.

title: A Small Pagan Book Club
premise: A fictional occult reading group accidentally summons its own literary critic.
pressure: A small occult book club has accidentally summoned the most exacting literary critic in existence. The entity hates lazy characterization.
investigate: Ask which book the critic believes is real
success: A marginal note points to a library copy of a future county charter.
failure: The critic tears up its own footnotes and vanishes before giving a recommendation.
help: Let the members choose the ending of their own story
helpOutcome: The critic admits that their imperfect, honest ending is better than its flawless one.
